summary: Iter100 RE-TEST of the 3 flagged fixes. P0 (frontend override dialog for customer-side fields) VERIFIED: Shortage, Excess and Halting manual overrides each open OverrideReasonDialog with the correct pure system value, Confirm is disabled until a reason is typed, and after Confirm the POST /api/trips/{id}/field-override audit entry persists (verified via GET /api/trips/{id}). P1 (PDF Basis='Fixed' when freight_mode=fixed even with a per_ton_loading snapshot) VERIFIED. P1 (single-trip invoice fits ONE landscape A4 page) VERIFIED with PyMuPDF page_count==1 plus all footer sections present on page 1. Regression: supplier-side override flow (supplier_freight + supplier_halting_amount) still opens the dialog and writes the audit trail; backend suites iter22 (7), iter23 (6), iter44 (4), iter82 (3), iter99 (1) = 23/23 PASS, plus iter100 suite 9/9 PASS and new iter100b suite 2/2 PASS. iter41 expenditure-breakdown skipped per instructions.

minor.issue: Manual supplier_freight override is silently discarded: when supplier_freight_mode='per_ton', _compute always recomputes supplier_freight = qty * rate. UI override of 16000 -> 15000 produced an audit entry (final_value=15000) but the stored supplier_freight stayed 16000, so the audit trail contradicts the persisted value. Pre-existing (not introduced by iter100) but it makes the new override audit misleading for supplier freight.

Cosmetic/UX: re-editing a trip that already has a persisted customer-side override re-prompts for a reason on every subsequent save (the pre-existing override row reappears in the dialog, and when shortage qty becomes 0 the row shows System=Rs 0.00 vs Final=old manual value). Consider skipping fields whose captured reason already exists in field_overrides.

action_items: Optional: honour a manual supplier_freight override in services.py (e.g. supplier_freight_override flag) so the stored value matches the audit entry.
Optional UX: do not re-prompt for a reason on fields that already carry a persisted field_overrides entry with the same final_value.
critical_code_review_comments: TripForm.detectOverrides() now correctly compares against pure system values (shortageAmountSystem / excessAmountSystem / haltingAmountSystem) - RCA from iteration_81 is resolved.
pdf/invoice.py _resolve_freight_basis() correctly prioritises freight_mode='fixed' over the applied_freight_method snapshot; compact layout keeps single-trip invoices on one landscape A4 page.
HaltingSection.jsx chargeable-days/halting manual toggle had no data-testid - added data-testid='trip-halting-amount-toggle' (test-only change).

success_rate.backend: 100% (34/34 across iter100, iter100b, iter22, iter23, iter44, iter82, iter99)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (4/4 override flows: shortage, excess, halting, supplier)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter100 is complete. Override dialog verification is easiest by seeding a trip via API (see /app/backend/tests/_iter100_seed_fe_trip.py) then opening /trips/{id}/edit, toggling the manual button (trip-shortage-amount-toggle / trip-excess-amount-toggle / trip-halting-amount-toggle) and clicking save-trip-btn. Note the dialog re-prompts for pre-existing overrides, so use a FRESH trip per field. Note also that manual supplier_freight is recomputed server-side (services.py:184). iter41 expenditure-breakdown truncation bug remains open and out of scope.
rca_of_the_issue: Previous defects are fixed: (1) detectOverrides() compared override-aware *Live values with themselves -> now compares pure system values, so customer-side dialogs fire; (2) _resolve_freight_basis() trusted the applied_freight_method snapshot over freight_mode -> now freight_mode='fixed' wins, Basis shows 'Fixed'; (3) invoice layout padding pushed the footer to page 2 -> compact spacing + KeepTogether keeps single-trip invoices at page_count==1.
